verdict.rationale: a-Shell offers its own non-interactive automation surfaces. Apple Shortcuts actions (Execute Command, Put File, Get File) run commands programmatically, optionally "in Extension", though the docs warn this won't always work. An optional built-in relay HTTPS server also accepts POST /run command lines. It is still an iOS app with no CI runner, headless binary or test environment, so CI-style automation is only approximated. Missing for 10: CI/pipeline integration, a true headless/CLI mode outside the iOS app, reliable documented background execution, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: `Execute Command`, which takes a list of commands and executes them in order. The input can also be a file or a text node
You can force a specific shortcut to run "in App" or "in Extension", with the warning that it won't always work.
POST /run takes a UTF-8 command line as its body and requires Content-Length and X-Token
You can write complex Shortcuts to download, process and release files using a-Shell commands.
